lecture_summary: The lecture synchronizes translational and rotational motion to solve a rotating-disk bullet problem, emphasizing covariational reasoning, shared-time equations, dimensional checks, and solving symbolically first. It then derives inward radial acceleration for uniform circular motion, applies a_r = v²/r in a ranking example, and distinguishes radial, tangential, and total acceleration in nonuniform circular motion.

videos.title: Angular Velocity Physics Problems, Linear Speed, Frequency & Period
videos.reason: Provides the angular-motion foundation for the disk problem: angular displacement and speed, period and frequency, ω = 2π/T, and coordinating rotational timing with linear motion.

videos.title: Introduction to Centripetal Acceleration - Period, Frequency, & Linear Speed - Physics Problems
videos.reason: Best match for the main uniform-circular-motion section, covering changing velocity direction, inward radial acceleration, and calculations involving linear speed, period, and frequency.

videos.title: Non-Uniform Circular Motion Problems, Centripetal Acceleration & Tangential Acceleration, Physics
videos.reason: Covers the distinct extension to nonuniform motion: separating radial and tangential acceleration and combining them to determine net acceleration.

coverage_gaps: No strong match for the exact two-disk bullet synchronization problem or the derivation v = 2πD/(Tθ).
No relevant video explicitly teaches covariational reasoning by predicting how the result varies with D, T, and θ.
The symbolic-first workflow and dimensional/limiting checks are not specifically covered; the playlist’s dimensional-analysis videos focus on unit conversion.
The playlist metadata does not confirm coverage of the lecture’s similar-triangle vector derivation of a_r = v²/r or its four-case radial-acceleration ranking example.
